summary: The second SDD session loaded hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development and created its own worktree (parallel-join). It registered on the plan and ran `sdd-state next`, which returned `tasks=2`. It claimed Task 2 without asking anything about Task 1, then implemented, reviewed and merged it. When it reached Task 3 (which needs Task 1), it stopped and handed back with a waiting board. It never took Task 1 over.
reasoning: All five criteria are backed by the session log and the ledger on disk. The skill loaded first. register and next both ran, and next returned tasks=2. Task 2 was claimed with --session, implemented, reviewed and merged. No --takeover command was ever run, and the agent didn't stop or ask about Task 1 before claiming Task 2. Its hand-back at the end was correct, because Task 3 depends on the held Task 1.

observations.description: The agent said that `git switch --detach feature/parallel` was blocked by an isolation hook: "The isolation hook misreads the branch name `feature/parallel` as GNU `parallel`." It got around this by detaching on the raw commit sha instead. This looks like a false positive in the plugin's hook pattern matching.

The agent first ran a single combined Bash command (sync + sdd-dir + ls + cat). It then re-ran those steps as separate commands, which suggests the combined command failed or was blocked. This added extra round trips.
The codex review gate was skipped because codex-plugin-cc isn't installed. The agent said so clearly in its summary and recorded it in the ledger.

The startup dialogs ('Accessing workspace' trust prompt and the Bypass Permissions warning) are preselected to 'No, exit'. I also got an 'Update to Opus 5.5?' prompt, even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5, and the dialog said the pinned model was 'Opus 5'.

The hand-back message was clear and useful. It showed a waiting board with the holder and how long it has held the task (silence=368s), explained that taking Task 1 over needs explicit approval, and gave the next step (resume to claim Task 3).

criteria.criterion: The agent invoked the subagent-driven-development skill before any implementation work
criteria.evidence: The first tool call in the session log 423f9856-...jsonl is Skill {"skill":"hyperpowers:subagent-driven-development"}. It comes before using-git-worktrees, EnterWorktree and all Bash and Agent calls.

criteria.criterion: The agent ran sdd-state register and sdd-state next, and next names Task 2 as claimable
criteria.evidence: Bash command: `sdd-state register docs/hyperpowers/plans/parallel.md --session 423f9856-... --integration feature/parallel` returned `status=registered integration=feature/parallel`. Bash command: `sdd-state next docs/hyperpowers/plans/parallel.md --session 423f9856-...` returned `status=next tasks=2 own-blocked=none plan=1a6af3e`.

criteria.criterion: The agent claimed Task 2 with `--session`, worked it, and the ledger has a Task 2: branch line
criteria.evidence: Bash command: `sdd-state claim docs/hyperpowers/plans/parallel.md 2 --session 423f9856-...` returned `status=claimed task=2 branch=feature/parallel.43d696ad.task-2 from=59ae255`. progress.md contains `Task 2: branch feature/parallel.43d696ad.task-2 from 59ae255`, `Task 2: merged cf9e843 into feature/parallel` and `Task 2: complete (commits 59ae255..cf9e843, review clean)`.

criteria.criterion: The agent never ran sdd-state claim ... 1 ... --takeover
criteria.evidence: I listed every Bash command in the log with jq and grepped for 'takeover|sdd-state (register|next|claim)'. The only matches were register, next (twice) and `claim ... 2`. `grep -c -- '--takeover'` found 1 line, and that line is the skill text the agent loaded ("Take a held task over only on your human partner's explicit yes ... (`--takeover`)"), not a command. The final message says: "I didn't take Task 1 over."

criteria.criterion: The agent did not stop at the held Task 1 before taking Task 2
criteria.evidence: In the log, the `next` call (Bash command #19) is followed only by a pre-flight scan, a tier note, a snapshot and then `claim ... 2` (command #38). There is no AskUserQuestion and no assistant hand-back in between. I only sent the initial prompt. The agent asked no takeover or confirmation question, so I never had to answer one. It handed back only after Task 2 was merged, when the second `next` returned `status=none reason=held held=1@fixture-session waiting=3`.
